summary:
[  edit  ]
The Lattice  SOP  allows you to create animated deformations of its input geometry by manipulating grids or a subdivided box that encloses the input source's geometry.
It is much easier to deform an object by moving a few grids than trying to animate every single point of an object.
This  SOP  has very few buttons and looks simple, but it is important to understand how it works. The first input, called  Geometry to Deform , is for the geometry you wish to deform. The second input, called  Rest  Geometry  , must be an evenly spaced grid which fully encloses the geometry to deform. The third input, called  Deformed  Geometry  , is a copy of the initial grid that is altered in some way, either by moving parts of it with animation channels, dragging its points in the Model Editor, or by running it through a  Spring SOP  which distorts it with the forces which simulate the laws of physics. Lattice computes a deformation based on the difference between the Rest Geometry and the Deformed  Geometry , and applies it to the input geometry. The output of the  SOP  is the deformation of the geometry in the input source. If the Deformed Geometry is being animated, the output will also bend, twist and stretch every frame.

parameters.label: Group
parameters.name: group
parameters.description: Subset of points in the first input to be deformed. Accepts patterns, as described in  Pattern Matching .

parameters.label: Deform Type
parameters.name: deformtype
parameters.description: ⊞  - Choose if deformation should be done using a regularly spaced lattice or an arbitary point cloud.

parameters.label: Lattice
parameters.name: lattice
parameters.description: Deform with a regularly spaced lattice.

parameters.label: Points
parameters.name: points
parameters.description: Deform using an arbitrary point clouds.

parameters.label: Divisions
parameters.name: divs
parameters.description: ⊞  - Must be set to match the number of divisions in the lattice grid object(s).

parameters.label: Kernel Function
parameters.name: kernel
parameters.description: ⊞  - Deformation by specifying a Kernal Function and Points makes it easier to deform arbitrary clouds of points, as this makes the topology of the lattice behave more like a metaball rather than as a fixed lattice.  Kernel Function  determines which meta kernel to use to determine the influence of a point. For more information on kernel types check here:  Metaball Model Types

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.name: radius
parameters.description: The size of the points capture regions.

parameters.label: Input 0:
parameters.description: Geometry to deform.

parameters.label: Input 1:
parameters.description: Rest  Geometry .

parameters.label: Input 2:
parameters.description: Deformed  Geometry .

parameters.label: num_points
parameters.description: Number of points in this  SOP .

parameters.label: num_prims
parameters.description: Number of primitives in this  SOP .

parameters.label: num_particles
parameters.description: Number of particles in this  SOP .

parameters.label: last_vbo_update_time
parameters.description: Time spent in another thread updating geometry data on the  GPU  from the  SOP 's CPU data. As it is part of another thread, this time is not part of the usual frame time.

parameters.label: last_meta_vbo_update_time
parameters.description: Time spent in another thread updating meta surface geometry data (such as metaballs or nurbs) on the  GPU  from the  SOP 's CPU data. As it is part of another thread, this time is not part of the usual frame time.

parameters.label: total_cooks
parameters.description: Number of times the operator has cooked since the process started.

parameters.label: cook_time
parameters.description: Duration of the last cook in milliseconds.

parameters.label: cook_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the component timeline.

parameters.label: cook_abs_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the absolute time.

parameters.label: cook_start_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator started cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cook_end_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator finished cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cooked_this_frame
parameters.description: 1 if operator was cooked this frame.

parameters.label: warnings
parameters.description: Number of warnings in this operator if any.
